correctness.rationale: Necessity follows from an exact fiber decomposition: after A=4X and B=4(1-Y), the target support forces A-B to be an odd integer, hence A and B share a fractional part. Conditional on that fractional part, uniformity forces a 4x4 matrix with every row and column sum 1/4, immediately bounding the two extreme diagonals. Sufficiency is constructive: the displayed nonnegative matrix has the required row/column sums and exactly the four desired diagonal totals. The derivation covers all boundary masses and uses no finite experiment as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating paper singles out the unresolved dimension-two aggregate-law problem and stops its discrete exact classifications at two and three atoms. The quarter-grid is not an arbitrary numerical slice: it is the smallest centered lattice scale at which all four offsets {-3,-1,1,3} can occur in the common-fractional-part reduction, so it is the first genuinely four-atomic member of that natural sequence. The result gives a complete two-parameter feasible polytope and an explicit coupling, showing that the sharp outer pointwise constraints become jointly sufficient on this family.
